title: Chronological
principle: The story’s order: each book placed where its events fall, by Wellspring’s own arrangement.

source.name: Wellspring’s arrangement (2026). Placements follow the text’s own headings where it has them — a psalm’s superscription, a prophet’s named kings, Ezra 5:1 — and are listed where it does not.

caveat: Publishers differ on Job, the Psalms, the prophets and the letters; this is one arrangement, Wellspring’s, and every placement is shown where it is made.
sequence: Job, placed after Genesis 11 in this arrangement: the book names no date; its world is the patriarchs’.
Psalm 90 — “A Prayer of Moses” — placed after Deuteronomy.
Psalm 59, whose heading names the night Saul watched David’s house (1 Samuel 19).
Psalms 56 and 34, whose headings name Gath and Abimelech (1 Samuel 21).
Psalms 52, 57 and 142: Doeg, and the cave (1 Samuel 22).
Psalms 54 and 63: the Ziphites, and the wilderness of Judah (1 Samuel 23).
Psalm 60, whose heading names the war with Aram and Edom (2 Samuel 8).
Psalm 51 — “when Nathan the prophet came unto him” (2 Samuel 12).
Psalm 3 — “when he fled from Absalom his son” (2 Samuel 15).
Psalm 18, the song of 2 Samuel 22, read beside it.
1 Chronicles, placed after 2 Samuel: the same reign told again, from the temple’s side.
The Psalter, placed after David’s reign: the psalms whose headings name an event are read at it; the rest are read here, in their own order.
Psalms 72 and 127, “of Solomon”, with his reign.
Proverbs, Ecclesiastes and the Song, ascribed to Solomon in their headings, placed in his reign.
Jonah, placed after 2 Kings 14, which names him under Jeroboam II (14:25).
Amos, whose heading names Uzziah and Jeroboam II.
Hosea, whose heading runs from Uzziah to Hezekiah; placed at Uzziah’s death.
Micah, whose heading names Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah.
Isaiah, whose heading names Uzziah to Hezekiah, placed whole after Hezekiah’s reign (Isaiah 36–39 retells 2 Kings 18–20).
Nahum names no king; placed before Josiah, as Nineveh fell in his reign.
Habakkuk names no king; placed at the rise of the Chaldeans, after Josiah.
Jeremiah, from Josiah’s thirteenth year to the fall; placed before 2 Kings 25, which its last chapter retells.
Lamentations, after the fall of Jerusalem.
Obadiah names no king; placed after the fall, which it seems to see.
Ezekiel, dated by the years of Jehoiachin’s exile, placed whole after the fall.
Daniel, from Jehoiakim’s third year to Cyrus, placed whole after Ezekiel.
2 Chronicles, the kings told again from the temple’s side, placed whole before Ezra, which continues its last verses.
Psalm 126, “when the LORD turned again the captivity of Zion”.
Haggai and Zechariah, whom Ezra 5:1 names at the rebuilding.
Esther, under Ahasuerus (Xerxes), placed between Ezra 6 (Darius) and Ezra 7 (Artaxerxes).
Malachi, placed with Nehemiah’s reforms, which it seems to share.
Joel names no king. Placed last among the prophets, as many modern readers date it after the exile; older readers place it under Joash.
Luke first: he says he set things down “in order” (1:3). The four Gospels are read whole, not cut into a harmony.
James names no date; placed early, by tradition.
Galatians, placed after the council of Acts 15.
The Thessalonian letters, placed after Paul’s visit in Acts 17.
The Corinthian letters and Romans, placed in the Ephesus and Corinth years of Acts 18–20.
The prison letters, placed at the Roman imprisonment where Acts ends.
The letters to Timothy and Titus, placed after Acts, which knows nothing of them.
The letters of Peter, Hebrews, Jude and John name no place in the story; placed after Paul’s letters, in canonical order.
